Within the documented organization-assignment scope and supported Copilot surfaces
Only to users who manually copy the patterns into local settings

questions.correctLabel: Within the documented organization-assignment scope and supported Copilot surfaces
questions.rationaleHtml:
Organization exclusions have a defined assignment scope and feature support. Copilot CLI and IDE Agent mode are documented exceptions.

Reference: Excluding content from GitHub Copilot - GitHub Docs

questions.promptHtml: A compliance team asks whether content exclusion guarantees that excluded code can never affect a Copilot response indirectly. What is accurate?

options.label: Yes, exclusion is a semantic-isolation guarantee for every Copilot feature
Yes, because exclusion retrains the underlying model
No; IDE semantic information can expose indirect details, and Copilot CLI plus IDE Agent mode do not support content exclusion

questions.correctLabel: No; IDE semantic information can expose indirect details, and Copilot CLI plus IDE Agent mode do not support content exclusion
questions.rationaleHtml:
GitHub documents both indirect semantic-information limitations and Copilot surfaces that do not support content exclusion.

questions.promptHtml: An administrator wants to test that content exclusions are working correctly before deploying them organization-wide. What validation approach is recommended?

options.label: Deploy exclusions immediately to production without testing
Configure exclusions in a test repository, verify that Copilot doesn't suggest content from excluded files, then roll out to organization
Ask GitHub Support to validate exclusions on their behalf

questions.correctLabel: Configure exclusions in a test repository, verify that Copilot doesn't suggest content from excluded files, then roll out to organization
questions.rationaleHtml:
Testing content exclusions in a controlled environment ensures patterns work correctly before organization-wide deployment, preventing unintended blocks or gaps.

questions.rationaleHtml:
GitHub does not claim ownership of input or output. Users must still evaluate generated material and comply with applicable law and third-party rights.

questions.rationaleHtml:
Basic troubleshooting starts with verifying configuration: IDE extension enabled, GitHub authentication valid, and active Copilot subscription.

questions.promptHtml: A developer finds that content exclusions seem to be blocking more files than intended. How should they diagnose this issue?

options.label: Review configured glob patterns for overly broad matches and test patterns against file paths to ensure precision
Disable all content exclusions permanently
Contact their manager to override exclusions

questions.rationaleHtml:
Overly broad exclusion patterns can unintentionally block needed context; reviewing and testing patterns ensures exclusions are precise and targeted.

questions.promptHtml: An administrator needs to verify that a content exclusion pattern works as intended. Which test is appropriate?

options.label: Assume every Copilot surface honors exclusion identically
Send real credentials in a prompt to test whether a proxy removes them
Use a supported IDE surface to compare behavior in excluded and non-excluded files after allowing propagation and refreshing the IDE

questions.correctLabel: Use a supported IDE surface to compare behavior in excluded and non-excluded files after allowing propagation and refreshing the IDE
questions.rationaleHtml:
A controlled test should verify the documented control without exposing real secrets. Results must be interpreted in light of unsupported surfaces and propagation time.

questions.rationaleHtml:

questions.promptHtml: Copilot returns an implementation that does not meet a developer’s requirements. Which prompt revision is most likely to improve the next response?

options.label: Repeat the identical vague request in uppercase
Add concrete requirements, relevant context, constraints, and an example of the expected result
Remove acceptance criteria so the model has more freedom

questions.correctLabel: Add concrete requirements, relevant context, constraints, and an example of the expected result
questions.rationaleHtml:
Effective prompts give Copilot enough specific context and constraints to produce a relevant, verifiable response. Iteration should clarify what was missing.

questions.rationaleHtml:
AI-generated test data requires human review. Synthetic values should satisfy the schema without copying personal or confidential production data.
